div.head: Hl 1
div.ab: Gif mannes esne eorlcundne mannan ofslæhð, þane ðe sio þreom hundum scll' gylde, se agend þone banan agefe ⁊ do þær þrio manwyrð to.
Gif mannes esne eorlcundne mannan ofslæhð þane ðe sio þreom hundum scll' gylde, se agend þone banan agefe ⁊ do þær þrio manwyrð to.
Gif mannes esne eorlcundne mannan ofslæhð, þane ðe sio þreom hundum sciƚƚ gylde, se agend þone banan agefe ⁊ do þær þrio manwyrð to.

Wenn jemandes Knecht einen adlig geborenen Menschen erschlägt, [nämlich] einen, welcher steht im 300 Schil.-[Wer]gelde, [so] liefere der [unschuldige] Eigenthümer [des Knechtes] diesen Todtschläger [an des Erschlagenen Sippe] aus und füge da drei Knechtspreise hinzu.

If someone’s servant slays a nobly born person, [namely] one who stands at a 300-shilling [wer]geld, [then] let the [innocent] owner [of the servant] hand over this killer [to the slain man’s kin] and add three slave-prices to it.
If a man’s servant slays a nobleman, whose wergeld is 300 shillings, his owner shall surrender the homicide and pay the value of three men in addition.
If a man’s servant kills a man of noble birth, who has a wergild of 300 shillings, the owner is to give up the slayer and pay in addition the value of three men.
If a person’s servant kills a man of noble birth, who should be compensated for with three hundred shillings, the owner should give up that killer and add three man-worths.

note.label: supplements
note.quote: Hlothere's first four clauses are a balanced pair, supplementing Æthelberht's final laws and revealing the nobleman's previously unwritten wergeld.

note.seg: Vermutlich Unfreier (s. d. Gl 1 e D) allgemein, den þeow mit umfassend. — Dem c. 1 entspricht in der Formel c. 3
Presumably the unfree man (see that word in Gl 1 e D) in general, including the þeow. — In its formula c. 1 corresponds to c. 3
‘Mann’, wie Frühere übersetzen, ist zunächst gemeint, aber nicht ausschliesslich; s. Gl Frau 1
‘Man’, as earlier translators render it, is meant primarily, but not exclusively; see Gl Frau 1
Dieselbe Formel der Standesbezeichnung u. 3
The same formula for designating rank below 3

S. Wb Optativ 10. Zur früheren Übersetzung ‘dann sei der Engelt 300 Sch.’ müsste man þe streichen, gyld lesen, þreo hund ändern. Richtig fiel dabei Price auf, dass der Zahler erst im folgenden Satz erschiene. Dieser, Thorpe, Toller 849a Z. 10 verbinden þane þe sio ‘whoever it be’, im Sinn des Relativum generale, der wohl für sy þe hit sy (s. Wb 183, Sp. 1 letzte Zeile), aber nicht hierfür, ohne sy und hit, belegt ist. Was sollte solcher Pleonasmus bedeuten? [In Lex Frision. 13 steht zwar cuiuscunque conditionis fuerit occisus, aber da kann die Tötung treffen nobilem, liberum, litum, nicht wie hier nur éine Klasse.] Der Unfreie kann keine 300 Schill. zahlen und erscheint nicht als Beklagter im Gericht; wenigstens zunächst trägt gegenüber der Aussenwelt der Herr die Haftung (s. d. Gl 6) für die Zahlung. Thorpe möchte, die Interpunktion ändernd, gylde se agend verbinden. Dann fehlt dahinter ‘und’. Diese Auslegung ist aus sachlichen Gründen unmöglich: die Tat würde ausser durch Wergeld noch durch Auslieferung und 3 Knechtspreise gebüsst werden, also weit strenger als wäre sie von Freien begangen. Dies widerspricht sowohl dem Rechte der Unfreien (s. d. Gl 17) wie dem der Haftung (s. d. Gl 6), die überall sonst durch Preisgebung (s. d. Gl) des Schuldigen sinkt oder schwindet. — Unmöglich ist auch Seebohm’s Deutung (Tribal Agsax. 474): ‘one who is now — zu halbem Wergeld, weil vom Sklaven getötet — paid for at 300 sh., let the owner in future usw.’

See Wb Optativ 10. For the earlier translation ‘then let the compensation be 300 shill.’ one would have to delete þe, read gyld and alter þreo hund. Price rightly noticed in this connection that the payer would then appear only in the following sentence. He, Thorpe and Toller 849a l. 10 take þane þe sio together as ‘whoever it be’, in the sense of the general relative, a sense which is indeed attested for sy þe hit sy (see Wb 183, col. 1 last line), but not for this, without sy and hit. What would such a pleonasm mean? [Lex Frision. 13 does indeed have cuiuscunque conditionis fuerit occisus, but there the killing may strike a nobilem, liberum, litum, not, as here, only one class.] The unfree man cannot pay 300 shill. and does not appear as defendant in court; at least in the first instance it is the lord who bears liability (see that word in Gl 6) for the payment towards the outside world. Thorpe, altering the punctuation, would take gylde se agend together. Then ‘and’ is missing after it. This interpretation is impossible on substantive grounds: the deed would be atoned for not only by wergild but also by surrender and 3 slave-prices, and thus far more severely than if it had been committed by freemen. This contradicts both the law of the unfree (see that word in Gl 17) and that of liability (see that word in Gl 6), which everywhere else is reduced or disappears through surrender (see that word in Gl) of the guilty party. — Also impossible is Seebohm’s interpretation (Tribal Agsax. 474): ‘one who is now — at half wergild, because killed by a slave — paid for at 300 sh., let the owner in future etc.’
gield (s. d. Wb 103) heisst ‘Wergeld’ auch sonst. Über den Instrumental des Preises s. Koch Engl. Gram. II § 113f.
gield (see that word in Wb 103) means ‘wergild’ elsewhere too. On the instrumental of price see Koch Engl. Gram. II § 113f.

Der Herr gilt in 1. 3 als unbeteiligt an der Missetat (vgl. Lex Frision. I 13) und unterliegt der Haftung nur, weil der Unfreie teilweise als Sache nicht selbst verantwortlich ist; dagegen in 2. 4 ist er der Begünstigung verdächtig

In 1. 3 the lord is regarded as having no part in the misdeed (cf. Lex Frision. I 13) and is subject to liability only because the unfree man, being in part a chattel, is not himself responsible; in 2. 4, by contrast, he is suspected of harbouring the offender
Der Herr hat nicht die Wahl, ihn auch, etwa gegen Zahlung des Sklavenpreises, zu behalten. Die Preisgebung steht der Todesstrafe gleich, auch bei Franken; Sohm Prozess 177
The lord does not have the option of keeping him instead, say against payment of the slave’s price. Surrender is equivalent to the death penalty, among the Franks too; Sohm Prozess 177
Im Agsä. nicht ‘Wergeld’
In A.-S. not ‘wergild’
The sentence þane ðe sio þreom hundum scll' gylde is probably merely explanatory—three hundred shillings being the wergeld of a Kentish nobleman. For the meaning of esne see note 1, Abt. cap. 85.

Not the wergeld of 3 freemen (which is the amount of the nobleman’s wergeld), but the value of 3 slaves (see Liebermann’s note ad loc.). This would be a much smaller sum. In Wessex (see Ine, cap. 74) the master of a Welsh slave who murders an Englishman is bound only to give up the slave, or pay his value (60 shillings).
Cap. 1. 3 are misunderstood by Schmid and Seebohm (Tribal Custom in A.S. Law, p. 467 ff.).
